description_en: Aśikharatemple at the Bhurtī Temple Complex which comprises 22śikharatemples (ordevala) and one stone fountain. Architectural activity at the site can be dated to the 13th-15thcenturies, corresponding to the late Khaśa Malla empire and the early phase of the Rāskoṭi dynasty (Andolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 128-129,Sharma 1972: 23-31,Sharma 2012: 120-123).The monument is built on a stone platform. It faces south, as most other temples in Bhurtī. The sanctum is currently empty but a circular cavity indicates that it probably once contained aśivaliṅga.The top part of the temple, which is traditionally surmounted by twoāmalakarings, now has a single ring, of recent origin. According to local informants the work was supervised by the Department of Archaeology and executed by stone sculptors from Bhaktapur.In 2008, the “Bhurti Temple Complex of Dailekh” was included in UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Restored
